class.name: NetwDespawnOpts
class.description: Carries the knobs that control teardown behavior. It is a record rather than an argument list so a new option can be added without breaking call sites, and its defaults are what make a despawn safe when a caller passes nothing. [codeblock] var opts := NetwDespawnOpts.create(&"killed") opts.linger = true NetwEntity.of(self).despawn(opts) [/codeblock]

method.name: create
method.description: Returns a record naming [param reason], leaving every other option at its default.

members.member: When [code]true[/code] (default), the [method Node.queue_free] call is deferred. This guarantees the engine's next process step sees the authority change before the node leaves the tree, which fixes the race where a [MultiplayerSynchronizer] tries to push state from a freed authority peer.

When [code]true[/code] (default), [method NetwPersistenceEngine.flush] runs on the despawning entity before authority revert and queue_free. A non-OK return is logged at error level and the despawn proceeds, so from the caller's perspective despawn is infallible.

When [code]true[/code], the entity deactivates now but is freed only after [member linger_seconds], so a late shooter can still validate against where it was. Its [NetwTimeline] freezes at the despawn boundary and expires when the node frees. Default [code]false[/code] keeps the cheap rule: you cannot be shot after the server saw you die.
Seconds a lingering entity stays rewindable before it frees. Sized to the server rewind retention window, roughly one second of ticks. Ignored unless [member linger] is [code]true[/code].

Recorded on the despawn span and forwarded to the [signal NetwEntity.despawning] signal so user code can branch on the cause. Common values: [code]&"peer_disconnected"[/code], [code]&"killed"[/code], [code]&"collected"[/code], [code]&"timeout"[/code].
